CZ-2025-05 – Conditional Zoning Map Amendment – A portion of 630 Irene Avenue, a portion 13 
of 1225 McLain Road, an Unaddressed parcel on Irene Avenue, and a portion of an 14 
Unaddressed parcel on Sweet Gum Street 15 
 16 
Assistant Planning Director Elizabeth McCarty provided details for case #CZ-2025-05, attached and 17 
made part of these minutes; and identified the applicant, address, and size of the property. She stated 18 
that the case is continued from the December 2025 meeting at the applicant’s request to ensure their 19 
attendance. Ms. McCarty stated that the request is to  conditionally rezone  four properties  20 
approximately 3.494 acres in total located at  a portion of 630 Irene Avenue, a portion of 1225 21 
McLain Road, an Unaddressed parcel on Irene Avenue, and a portion of an Unaddressed parcel on 22 
Sweet Gum Street. The properties are currently zoned City of Kannapolis General Commercial (GC) 23 
and Residential 8 (R8) zoning districts and the request is to assign City of Kannapolis Residential -24 
18 (R18-CZ) zoning district for a 52-unit multi-family development.  25 
 26 
Ms. McCarty shared that the proposed project has wastewater allocation under affordable housing, 27 
and is also a redevelopment of a brownfield site.  28 
 29 
Ms. McCarty directed the Commission’s attention to case maps, further illustrating the location, 30 
current and surrounding zoning districts, existing property uses, as well as the Character Area as 31 
determined by the Move Kannapolis Forward 2030 Comprehensive Plan (“2030 Plan”). She further 32 
directed the Commission’s attention to site photos, stating that staff found consistency with the 2030 33 
Plan and is recommending approval of the rezoning request with the following conditions: 34 
 35 
1. The permitted uses allowed by this rezoning shall be limited to those uses and accessory 36 
uses allowed by- right in the Residential 18 (R18) zoning district. The intent of this 37 
rezoning submittal is to provide for a multifamily development. 38 
2. The number of multifamily dwelling units shall not exceed 52 as depicted on the 39 
Rezoning Plan. 40 
3. The development depicted on the Rezoning Plan is schematic in nature and is intended 41 
to show the general arrangement of such uses and improvements on the site. Accordingly, 42 
the ultimate layout, locations and sizes of the development and site elements depicted on 43 
the Rezoning Plan are graphic representations, and they may be altered or modified in 44 
accordance with the City of Kannapolis Development Ordinance. 45

4. Perimeter buffer yards shall meet the requirements of the KDO. A Type A Buffer is 1

CARY, NORTH CAROLINA   FY 2024 4TH QUARTER REPORT
HIGGINS GREENWAY – PHASE 3
Cary began construction on phase 3 of the Higgins Greenway  
in April. The existing greenway will be extended 0.86 miles from 
its current terminus at Union Street eastward to Kildaire Farm 
Road. This work will fill a gap in the greenway network and 
increase connectivity between downtown Cary and the 
surrounding neighborhoods. The project is anticipated to  
continue through summer 2025.
BLACK CREEK GREENWAY  
AND CARY PARKWAY  
PHOTOGRAPHED RIGHT
Black Creek Greenway renovations and Cary Parkway  
sidewalk construction at Black Creek started on June 3. These 
projects will improve and rehabilitate Black Creek Greenway 
from West Dynasty Drive to Old Reedy Creek Road and 
complete a sidewalk gap along Cary Parkway over Black 
Creek. Construction is anticipated to take three years to complete 
and will take place in three phases to help minimize impacts to 
greenway users. Each phase will require closing and detouring 
that section of the greenway while the other sections of the 
greenway remain open. The first phase begins at West Dynasty 
Drive and ends at the North Cary Park access to the Black  
Creek Greenway.
GOCARY
The new GoCary Downtown Loop (DL) began June 1, providing 
more access to downtown attractions and parking options. 
Additionally, the microtransit feasibility study is wrapping up after 
1 9 community engagement events and 1,270 survey responses. 
Staff will present future service recommendations to Council later 
this summer.
